```python
from sklearn.linear_model import LogisticRegression
import numpy as np
import statsmodels.api as sm

# Prepare the data for logistic regression
X = df[['INCOME']].values.reshape(-1, 1)  # Predictor
y = df['SAMESAVE'].values  # Response

# Create a logistic regression model
model = LogisticRegression()
model.fit(X, y)

# Get the coefficient
coefficient = model.coef_[0][0]

# To calculate p-value, we need the standard error of the coefficient
# We can use statsmodels to get the standard error
X_sm = sm.add_constant(X)
model_sm = sm.Logit(y, X_sm)
result_sm = model_sm.fit()

# Get the standard error
std_error = result_sm.bse[1]

# Calculate the z-score
z_score = coefficient / std_error

# Calculate the p-value using the z-score
p_value = 2 * (1 - np.abs(z_score))

coefficient, p_value
```
